memory_update.text: For restaurant franchisors, the durable bottleneck may be franchisee return on invested capital, not just brand demand; supply-chain procurement, ad-fund efficiency, digital ordering, and remodel capex can determine whether new units keep opening.
DPZ should remain a reference-pattern company for vertically integrated franchisor economics: royalty stream plus advertising fund plus controlled supply-chain infrastructure.

WEST and FARM are underfollowed or speculative restaurant-supplier candidates to verify through customer concentration, foodservice revenue mix, capacity utilization, margin recovery, and balance-sheet risk.

node: Franchise royalty, advertising fund, and brand-system economics
summary: Layer 1B expands the node from franchisor royalty streams into the less obvious inputs that make franchise systems economically viable: vertically integrated food distribution, coffee/private-label beverage supply, direct-store-delivery networks, and equipment/remodel infrastructure. The best-supported reference pattern is Domino's, where franchise economics are reinforced by procurement scale and supply-chain infrastructure rather than royalties alone. The underfollowed lane centers on B2B suppliers whose revenue depends on restaurants, hospitality, and franchise systems continuing to open, remodel, and drive same-store sales.
